source_title: George Michael at His Eighties Pop Peak: See Photos From ‘The Faith Tour’
source_excerpt:
George Michael was in the midst of pulling off a stunning coup at the start of 1988. Already a proven hitmaker as one half of Wham!, he’d just released his debut solo album, Faith , including the provocative, ultra-catchy hits “Faith,” “Father Figure,” and “I Want Your Sex.” By the time he launched his first solo tour, in Tokyo that February, he was inarguably one of the biggest stars in the world. “I really think that anyone who doesn’t like anything on my new album has no right to say they like pop music,” Michael, 24, said that year in his first Rolling Stone cover story . The new film George Michael: The Faith Tour was shot on 35mm at two performances in Paris that spring, and the footage was long considered lost — until now. Here are some of the most striking images from the film, which arrives in theaters later this year. Tickets are on sale now .
Listen Up Image Credit: Michael Putland/Getty Images George Michael listens to a Walkman while riding a bullet train during the Japanese leg of his Faith World Tour in February 1988.

Behind the Camera Image Credit: Michael Putland “As you can see in the new trailer for The Faith Tour , his confidence was raging — night after night, he faced a crowd of strangers and sang the line, ‘If you ever hunger, hunger for me,’ making everyone in the room hear it as a personal demand,” Rolling Stone ‘s Rob Sheffield recently wrote . “For once, and only once, he was willing to live up to every crazed fantasy the world had about George Michael — and that includes his own secret fantasies about himself.”
